# Independent page-art border controls

`control.docx` is manually authored OOXML generated by
`tools/page_art_border_fixture.py`. It reuses only the repository's own minimal
OPC shell, has six 300x220pt sections, and contains no corpus artwork or embedded
fonts. `cases.json` records the authored side declarations. Regenerating the
package is deterministic.

Native reference: the reference application, read-only
`ExportAsFixedFormat`, six pages. The source SHA-256 was identical before and
after export. `native-measurements.json` records the reference PDF hash, graphical
bounds, RGB colors, command counts, and shape/clip hashes. It contains no copied
border paths, image tiles or font programs. The private PDF and all six rendered
pages were inspected; the PDF is not bundled.

Run `tools/inspect_page_art_reference.py REFERENCE.pdf --output measurements.json`
to regenerate the graphical measurements. This tool ignores text/font resources
and rejects curves, strokes and image XObjects rather than falsely asserting
equality for an unsupported reference. Run its three parser checks with
`python tools/test_page_art_reference.py`.

## Confirmed compatibility findings

- Uniform `handmade1` controls cover text/page-relative placement and sizes 7,
  21 and 31 points. Art widths use points, not the eighth-points of line borders.
- Page 6 declares top/left/bottom/right widths 7/14/21/31. All eight filled paths,
  their colors, bounds and clipping hashes are **exactly equal** to page 2, which
  declares width 7 on all four sides. The reference application does not apply independent art widths
  in this control. This is not a general precedence rule yet: top-only, reordered
  declarations and different art styles need further controls.
- Page 5 declares `handmade1` top/right and `single` left/bottom. The reference application paints eight
  art pieces, including art on left/bottom. Their bounds differ from page 1:
  the ordinary side widths affect the frame placement. A four-side ordinary-line
  painter cannot reproduce this result.
- Page 4 declares only a top border. The reference application paints three art pieces: the top edge
  and both upper corners, whose endcaps extend downward.
- Native ink is RGB approximately `(34,51,68)`, the authored `223344`. This
  conflicts with the §17.6.2 `color` statement that art borders ignore this
  attribute. It is confirmed for this monochrome style, not every art style.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.6.2, 17.6.10, 17.18.2 and normative Annex F define the
underlying border semantics. Annex F's electronic PNG files are present in the
user-supplied spec directory. `asset-manifest.json` records only the eight
`handmade1` tile names, dimensions and hashes. They have **not** been bundled:
the user's approval for Ecma's custom copyright terms is pending. They are not
MIT/Apache assets. The official policy is at
https://ecma-international.org/policies/by-ipr/ecma-text-copyright-policy/ .

## Remaining work

Rendering support is still missing. Do not remove the import guard merely because
these controls or their schemas pass. After asset approval, implement a generic
art-frame painter with independent held-out controls for edge/corner geometry,
style/size precedence, partial sides, color/theme, display/z-order and clipping;
verify text editing and original-package preservation. Other preset art borders
and relationship-defined custom borders remain separate missing capabilities.

Local validation: two source schema views, three graphical parser checks, and
18 existing page-border unit checks passed. No production behavior changed.
